clusters.blurb: The server, laptop, phone and cloud sessions that the system runs on.

clusters.name: AI agents
clusters.blurb: Assistants that plan work, capture ideas and consult other models.

clusters.name: Monitoring & workflow
clusters.blurb: The board, monitors and shared notes that help me keep work on track.

clusters.name: Smart home
clusters.blurb: Lights by voice, plus AC and plant watering projects in progress.

clusters.name: Portfolio

systems.name: Always-on server
systems.blurb: An old laptop running Linux around the clock. It hosts agents and home relays, and has a nightly backup.

systems.name: Dev laptop
systems.blurb: My daily machine, where I build with Claude Code and Codex and run helper agents.

systems.name: Phone + Siri
systems.blurb: Siri Shortcuts on my phone send simple web requests to the server so I can switch lights or start a task.

systems.name: AI in the cloud
systems.blurb: Claude and Codex sessions run scheduled jobs. AI can search the logs; the only actions it can take are sending me one alert and logging a job check-in.

systems.name: Igor (orchestrator agent)
systems.blurb: Igor is an always-on agent that builds my morning brief, takes voice notes and queues coding jobs. I use it through Telegram.

systems.name: Link-to-idea bot
systems.blurb: Share a short video from my phone and get back a transcript and an idea note matched to my projects.

systems.name: Helper agents
systems.blurb: Four smaller AI helpers cover research, verification, code and handoff notes.

systems.name: Second opinions
systems.blurb: I use a step that asks other AI models for a second opinion before big changes.

systems.name: Bot logs connector
systems.blurb: AI can search the logs; the only actions it can take are sending me one alert and logging a job check-in.

systems.name: Open Threads board
systems.blurb: One board for open tasks, like a support queue. Each item has a status, a priority and a next step.

systems.name: Morning sweep + nightly plan
systems.blurb: Scheduled runs collect loose ends each morning and plan the night’s unattended work each evening.

systems.name: Failure watcher
systems.blurb: A small script checks that jobs produce fresh results and alerts me when an output goes stale.

systems.name: Monthly health check
systems.blurb: A scheduled monthly run finds stale or broken parts, fixes what is safe to fix and lists the rest for me to decide.

systems.name: Usage tracker
systems.blurb: Collects how much AI capacity each tool uses so I can plan work around the limits.

systems.name: Shared context
systems.blurb: A shared set of rules and handoff notes so Claude and Codex can pick up each other’s work.

systems.name: Guardrail hooks
systems.blurb: I’m moving rules such as “never read secret files” out of prompts and into scripts that block the action.

systems.name: Lights by voice
systems.blurb: I say a phrase to Siri and the server switches bulbs and lamps through a small relay service.

systems.name: Plant watering
systems.blurb: Wireless soil sensors report moisture to the server; pumps and automatic watering to follow.

systems.name: AC by voice
systems.blurb: I’ve tested the manual shortcut that sends a command through an infrared blaster. The spoken Siri path still needs verification.

systems.name: This map
systems.blurb: An interactive map built from a small public data file. It shows a dated snapshot of the system.

systems.name: Portfolio site
systems.blurb: My portfolio, with case studies of Igor and a team web app.

systems.name: Trellife (team project)
systems.blurb: A Trello-style full-stack app built by a three-person bootcamp team. I deployed and run my own copy.
